effects: Sets the signer's LBTC allowance for `spender` to `value`, replacing any earlier allowance (OZ ERC20Upgradeable.approve). At max uint256 the allowance never goes down.
formats.shown: Shows "Approve", the amount with the token resolved from the contract ("Unlimited LBTC" above the threshold), and the spender.

findings.title: approve has no interpolatedIntent, so the intent line names neither the amount nor the spender.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json display.formats approve: "intent": "Approve" and no interpolatedIntent. Case 0 screen intent is just "Approve".

effects: Destroys `amount` of the signer's LBTC (StakedLBTC.burn calls _burn(_msgSender(), amount)). Nothing comes back: no BTC and no other token.
formats.shown: Shows "Burn" and the amount of LBTC to burn.

findings.title: burn's intent does not say the tokens are destroyed with nothing in return, unlike redeemForBtc.
findings.evidence: StakedLBTC.sol burn(uint256): `_burn(_msgSender(), amount);` with no payout. descriptor intent "Burn" sits next to "Redeem" and "Redeem BTC".

effects: Anyone can call it. It forwards rawPayload and proof to the AssetRouter (StakedLBTC.mint → $.assetRouter.mint), which mints StakedLBTC to a recipient and amount encoded in the payload. The signer pays no tokens. The recipient and amount live in the payload, not with the signer.
What the router does could not be checked from the source here.
formats.shown: Shows "Mint" and then the payload and the consortium proof as raw hex.

findings.title: mint shows the stake payload as raw bytes, so the recipient and amount it mints cannot be read.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json mint: field rawPayload format "raw"; StakedLBTC.sol mint(bytes,bytes) natspec: "rawPayload The message with the stake data"; return value `recipient` comes from the payload.
findings.fix: The spec cannot slice the packed payload, so add an interpolatedIntent such as "Mint staked LBTC for the deposit proven by this payload" and hide the proof.

findings.title: mint shows the consortium signature as raw hex, which tells the signer nothing.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json mint: field proof label "Proof" format "raw" visible "always"; natspec: "Signature of the consortium approving the mint".
findings.fix: Set the proof field to visible "never".

findings.title: mint: the recipient and amount are packed in the payload bytes, and no ERC-7730 format can decode them.
findings.evidence: StakedLBTC.sol mint(bytes,bytes) returns $.assetRouter.mint(rawPayload, proof); the AssetRouter source is not in the directory.

formats.key: permit(address owner, address spender, uint256 value, uint256 deadline, uint8 v, bytes32 r, bytes32 s)
effects: Sets `owner`'s LBTC allowance for `spender` to `value` from owner's EIP-2612 signature, and uses up owner's nonce (ERC20PermitUpgradeable.permit). The signer only submits it; owner may be someone else.
formats.shown: Shows "Permit", then the owner, spender, allowance ("Unlimited LBTC" above the threshold) and the deadline as a date. The signature parts are hidden.

findings.title: permit's intent "Permit" does not say it sets the owner's allowance for the spender.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json permit: "intent": "Permit", no interpolatedIntent. Case 1 screen intent "Permit".
findings.fix: Add interpolatedIntent "Allow {spender} to spend {value} of {owner}'s tokens until {deadline}".

effects: Calls $.assetRouter.redeem(_msgSender(), address(this), amount). This most likely takes `amount` StakedLBTC from the signer and creates a redemption to another asset, minus a redeem fee set in the router (getRedeemFee). The router code is not in the directory, so what arrives, when, and to whom could not be checked.
formats.shown: Shows "Redeem" and the amount of LBTC to redeem.

findings.title: redeem shows only the LBTC that leaves; it never says what the signer gets back or that a fee applies.
findings.evidence: StakedLBTC.sol redeem: `$.assetRouter.redeem(_msgSender(), address(this), amount);`; getRedeemFee() reads tokenConfig from the router. descriptor redeem: intent "Redeem" and one field "Amount to Redeem".
findings.fix: Name the asset received in the intent, e.g. "Redeem {amount} staked LBTC for LBTC (fee applies)", once the router behaviour is confirmed.

findings.title: redeem: the fee and exchange ratio come from the router's storage and cannot be shown.
findings.evidence: StakedLBTC.sol getRedeemFee(), ratio(), getRate() all read $.assetRouter.

effects: Calls $.assetRouter.redeemForBtc(msg.sender, this, scriptPubkey, amount), which burns `amount` StakedLBTC from the signer and queues a BTC payout to `scriptPubkey` on Bitcoin. The payout is the amount less the redeem fee or commission and converted at the router's ratio. The router code is not in the directory.
formats.shown: Shows "Redeem BTC", the LBTC amount to burn, and the Bitcoin scriptPubkey as raw hex.

findings.title: redeemForBtc shows the BTC destination as raw scriptPubkey hex, which no ERC-7730 format can turn into an address.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json redeemForBtc: field scriptPubkey label "ScriptPubKey (BTC)" format "raw".
findings.fix: None today. A Bitcoin address format would be needed.

findings.title: redeemForBtc: the BTC received is the burned amount less a fee and ratio stored in the router, so the screen cannot state it.
findings.evidence: StakedLBTC.sol calcUnstakeRequestAmount natspec: "amountAfterFee The amount that will be unstaked (after deducting the burn commission)"; toNativeCommission() and getRedeemFee() read the router.
findings.fix: Say "BTC received is net of the protocol fee" in the intent or label.

effects: Moves `value` LBTC from the signer to `to` (OZ ERC20 transfer). It reverts when the contract is paused.
formats.shown: Shows "Send", the amount of LBTC and the recipient.

findings.title: transfer's recipient types allow only eoa and wallet, but the code accepts any address, contracts included.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json transfer: to params types ["eoa","wallet"]; ERC20Upgradeable.transfer only rejects the zero address.
findings.fix: Add "contract" to the types or drop the types restriction.

formats.key: transferFrom(address from, address to, uint256 value)
effects: Moves `value` LBTC from `from` to `to`, and lowers the signer's allowance from `from` by `value` unless that allowance is unlimited (OZ ERC20 transferFrom).
formats.shown: Shows "Transfer", the amount, the from address and the recipient.

findings.title: transferFrom's from and recipient types allow only eoa and wallet, but contracts are valid parties.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json transferFrom: from and to params types ["eoa","wallet"]; ERC20Upgradeable.transferFrom only rejects zero addresses.
findings.fix: Add "contract" to the types or drop the types restriction.

couldNotCheck: AssetRouter: StakedLBTC.mint(bytes,bytes), redeem(uint256) and redeemForBtc(bytes,uint256) send all their work to $.assetRouter, an address held in storage. Neither its source nor the IAssetRouter interface is in the directory, so I could not confirm which tokens these calls burn, mint or pay out, to whom, or the fee deducted.
